doc.brief: Arranges its child widgets in rows and columns.
doc.md:
Arranges its child widgets in rows and columns.

It supports arbitrary positions and horizontal/vertical spans.

Children are added using [`Grid.attach()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:attach). They can span multiple
rows or columns. It is also possible to add a child next to an existing
child, using [`Grid.attach_next_to()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:attach_next_to). To remove a child from the
grid, use [`Grid.remove()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:remove).

The behaviour of `GtkGrid` when several children occupy the same grid
cell is undefined.

# GtkGrid as GtkBuildable

Every child in a `GtkGrid` has access to a custom [`Buildable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Buildable)
element, called `<layout>`. It can by used to specify a position in the
grid and optionally spans. All properties that can be used in the `<layout>`
element are implemented by [`GridLayoutChild`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GridLayoutChild).

It is implemented by `GtkWidget` using [`LayoutManager`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LayoutManager).

To showcase it, here is a simple example:

```xml
<object class="GtkGrid" id="my_grid">
  <child>
    <object class="GtkButton" id="button1">
      <property name="label">Button 1</property>
      <layout>
        <property name="column">0</property>
        <property name="row">0</property>
      </layout>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="GtkButton" id="button2">
      <property name="label">Button 2</property>
      <layout>
        <property name="column">1</property>
        <property name="row">0</property>
      </layout>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="GtkButton" id="button3">
      <property name="label">Button 3</property>
      <layout>
        <property name="column">2</property>
        <property name="row">0</property>
        <property name="row-span">2</property>
      </layout>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="GtkButton" id="button4">
      <property name="label">Button 4</property>
      <layout>
        <property name="column">0</property>
        <property name="row">1</property>
        <property name="column-span">2</property>
      </layout>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

It organizes the first two buttons side-by-side in one cell each.
The third button is in the last column but spans across two rows.
This is defined by the `row-span` property. The last button is
located in the second row and spans across two columns, which is
defined by the `column-span` property.

# CSS nodes

`GtkGrid` uses a single CSS node with name `grid`.

# Accessibility

Until GTK 4.10, `GtkGrid` used the [`AccessibleRole.group`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:group) role.

Starting from GTK 4.12, `GtkGrid` uses the [`AccessibleRole.generic`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:generic) role.

attach.brief: Adds a widget to the grid.
attach.md:
Adds a widget to the grid.

The position of `child` is determined by `column` and `row`.
The number of “cells” that `child` will occupy is determined
by `width` and `height`.

attach_next_to.brief: Adds a widget to the grid.
attach_next_to.md:
Adds a widget to the grid.

The widget is placed next to `sibling`, on the side determined by
`side`. When `sibling` is `NULL`, the widget is placed in row (for
left or right placement) or column 0 (for top or bottom placement),
at the end indicated by `side`.

Attaching widgets labeled `[1]`, `[2]`, `[3]` with `@sibling == `NULL`` and
`@side == %GTK_POS_LEFT` yields a layout of `[3][2][1]`.

get_baseline_row.brief: Returns which row defines the global baseline of `grid`.
get_baseline_row.md: Returns which row defines the global baseline of `grid`.

get_child_at.brief: Gets the child of `grid` whose area covers the grid cell at `column`, `row`.
get_child_at.md:
Gets the child of `grid` whose area covers the grid
cell at `column`, `row`.

get_column_homogeneous.brief: Returns whether all columns of `grid` have the same width.
get_column_homogeneous.md: Returns whether all columns of `grid` have the same width.

get_column_spacing.brief: Returns the amount of space between the columns of `grid`.
get_column_spacing.md: Returns the amount of space between the columns of `grid`.

get_row_baseline_position.md:
Returns the baseline position of `row`.

See [`Grid.set_row_baseline_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:set_row_baseline_position).

get_row_homogeneous.brief: Returns whether all rows of `grid` have the same height.
get_row_homogeneous.md: Returns whether all rows of `grid` have the same height.

get_row_spacing.brief: Returns the amount of space between the rows of `grid`.
get_row_spacing.md: Returns the amount of space between the rows of `grid`.

insert_column.brief: Inserts a column at the specified position.
insert_column.md:
Inserts a column at the specified position.

Children which are attached at or to the right of this position
are moved one column to the right. Children which span across this
position are grown to span the new column.

insert_next_to.brief: Inserts a row or column at the specified position.
insert_next_to.md:
Inserts a row or column at the specified position.

The new row or column is placed next to `sibling`, on the side
determined by `side`. If `side` is %GTK_POS_TOP or %GTK_POS_BOTTOM,
a row is inserted. If `side` is %GTK_POS_LEFT of %GTK_POS_RIGHT,
a column is inserted.

insert_row.brief: Inserts a row at the specified position.
insert_row.md:
Inserts a row at the specified position.

Children which are attached at or below this position
are moved one row down. Children which span across this
position are grown to span the new row.

query_child.brief: Queries the attach points and spans of `child` inside the given `GtkGrid`.
query_child.md: Queries the attach points and spans of `child` inside the given `GtkGrid`.

remove.md:
Removes a child from `grid`.

The child must have been added with
[`Grid.attach()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:attach) or [`Grid.attach_next_to()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Grid#method:attach_next_to).

remove_column.brief: Removes a column from the grid.
remove_column.md:
Removes a column from the grid.

Children that are placed in this column are removed,
spanning children that overlap this column have their
width reduced by one, and children after the column
are moved to the left.

remove_row.brief: Removes a row from the grid.
remove_row.md:
Removes a row from the grid.

Children that are placed in this row are removed,
spanning children that overlap this row have their
height reduced by one, and children below the row
are moved up.

set_baseline_row.brief: Sets which row defines the global baseline for the entire grid.
set_baseline_row.md:
Sets which row defines the global baseline for the entire grid.

Each row in the grid can have its own local baseline, but only
one of those is global, meaning it will be the baseline in the
parent of the `grid`.

set_column_homogeneous.brief: Sets whether all columns of `grid` will have the same width.
set_column_homogeneous.md: Sets whether all columns of `grid` will have the same width.

set_column_spacing.brief: Sets the amount of space between columns of `grid`.
set_column_spacing.md: Sets the amount of space between columns of `grid`.

set_row_baseline_position.brief: Sets how the baseline should be positioned on `row` of the grid, in case that row is assigned more space than is requested.
set_row_baseline_position.md:
Sets how the baseline should be positioned on `row` of the
grid, in case that row is assigned more space than is requested.

The default baseline position is %GTK_BASELINE_POSITION_CENTER.

set_row_homogeneous.brief: Sets whether all rows of `grid` will have the same height.
set_row_homogeneous.md: Sets whether all rows of `grid` will have the same height.

set_row_spacing.brief: Sets the amount of space between rows of `grid`.
set_row_spacing.md: Sets the amount of space between rows of `grid`.

baseline-row.brief: The row to align to the baseline when valign is using baseline alignment.
baseline-row.md: The row to align to the baseline when valign is using baseline alignment.

column-homogeneous.brief: If `TRUE`, the columns are all the same width.
column-homogeneous.md: If `TRUE`, the columns are all the same width.

column-spacing.brief: The amount of space between two consecutive columns.
column-spacing.md: The amount of space between two consecutive columns.

row-homogeneous.brief: If `TRUE`, the rows are all the same height.
row-homogeneous.md: If `TRUE`, the rows are all the same height.

row-spacing.brief: The amount of space between two consecutive rows.
row-spacing.md: The amount of space between two consecutive rows.
